home.aboutSummary: Architecture graduate of Drexel's 2+4 program, now managing adaptive reuse projects in Philadelphia. Most motivated by constraint-heavy problems and the creative solutions they demand.

paragraphs: Driven architecture graduate of the 2+4 program at Drexel University. A quick learner interested in implementing innovative and creative techniques in designing inclusive, community-oriented projects.

My strengths lie in early design and conceptual development — diagramming, rendering, and clearly conveying intent. I excel at communication and presentation, translating complex ideas into clear, compelling narratives. I am most motivated when tackling constraint-heavy problems, and most fulfilled when crafting creative, unique solutions.

I am seeking a civically minded, challenging role that prioritizes sustainability and community while providing opportunities to broaden my skills. I aim to help positively transform Philadelphia's built environment.

timeline.title: Project Manager / Designer, Philly Office Retail
timeline.detail: Adaptive reuse and state-of-good-repair projects from design through construction. Coordinating architects, contractors and consultants, overseeing budgets and schedules, leading RFPs and negotiations.

timeline.title: Designer, WRT Planning + Design
timeline.detail: Large-scale affordable mixed-use projects from proposal to 90% CDs. Research on biophilic design and energy modeling for carbon-negative communities, and renderings across housing and education projects.

timeline.title: Bachelor of Architecture, Drexel University
timeline.detail: Philadelphia, PA. Pearson Prize Silver Medal for best Drexel architectural thesis project.

routes.label: I'm hiring
routes.blurb: Naugatuck is the professional work — a mixed-use building for Pennrose, drawn at WRT and in construction now. For planning at the district scale, Pride in Place is the one to read: a whole neighborhood worked out from the street up, with the mapping and circulation studies behind it. Block Core and Kensington Core show a scheme developing from a single corner to a whole block. My résumé and references are on the About page.

routes.label: I'm an architect or designer
routes.blurb: Post Scarcity is the thesis, laid out as a walkthrough you can read straight through. Pride in Place carries the analysis — circulation studies, street modules, the research the plan answers to. Both have the drawings behind the renders.

routes.label: Just looking around
routes.blurb: Kensington Core has the films, if you would rather watch than read. Garden Schools is the one with the landscape. Otherwise sweep the timeline below and open whatever catches your eye — every project opens with its pictures.
